title: Parameter-dependent boundary coordinates and full source tests
source_hypothesis: Smooth scalar second-order coefficient family on compactly nested noncharacteristic boundary charts, real symmetric principal coefficients and arbitrary complex lower terms. One fixed positive density, original Banach embedding into extendible distributions, actual smooth zero-value inputs and full input-support margins. Coordinate and finite-list transfer allow zero tangential dimension; fixed scalar assembly additionally requires a positive-dimensional reference chart and its stated disjoint tangential reserve.
reviewed_arguments: H0–N0 use a fixed reference normal chart and one noncharacteristic parameter collar. The base flow preserves the defining function, is the identity on the boundary, eliminates the principal cross terms and has a common smooth inverse before any target order is chosen.
N1 computes the full nondivergence coordinate formula, including the inverse-coordinate Hessian with its negative-i sign. No definiteness of the tangential principal form is needed.

D0 gives the exact unitary density factor, its correctly ordered inverse and every first-order and potential correction. D1 divides on the left by the actual highest normal coefficient, without differentiating that multiplier.
G0 retains the complex gauge, full tangential conjugate, normal potential and exact source multiplier. The zero value trace is preserved with the actual boundary density factor.

K0 proves the compressed cotangent law and fixes compact cone margins before the order. It transfers generalized rays through the cotangent map and the actual positive time change, retaining the possible fixed orientation reversal.

K1 checks the whole resolved corner under the coordinate map: the lifted diagonal, conormal remainders, compact projections and infinite-order side-face flatness. All original residual kernels remain in the transferred tests.

B0 transposes the complete coordinate, density, gauge and cutoff map on flat tests. The original Banach embedding then gives a uniform negative Sobolev restriction bound, without assuming Banach invariance or a chosen linear extension.

T0 chooses the cutoff and coarse order before constructing the local estimate. Its full input projection condition makes the differential cutoff commutator vanish exactly after every actual source test. Microsupport separation alone is explicitly insufficient.

T1 gives exact unitary equalities for the original targets, source and observation terms, including the normalizing and gauge multipliers. The inverse prescription returns an arbitrary specified full target exactly.

C0 applies fixed scalar assembly only within one reference chart with the stated reserve and full-support margins. Actual graph injection and a conditional continuous Banach trace are proved by the earlier full-transpose argument.

Three complete solutions verify a constant shear, an exponential collar with a surviving tangential lower coefficient, and a degenerate principal form with the exact forcing factor and potential 13/16.

The current component scope paragraphs were visually inspected at desktop and mobile widths. All formulas parse, display and figure extents are accessible, and the component retains its stated hypotheses and actual tested-graph scope.
visual_review_scope: Current component scope paragraphs at desktop and mobile widths; all formula and figure extents measured.
